patch_description: The current per-sample Python loop computes weighted linear regression twice per output sample, which is slow (execution_time jumped from 0.01 to 0.05) and leaves slope churn high (slope_changes 256.6, false_reversals 200.2, smoothness 0.07). We vectorize the first-pass regression using np.convolve (Sx and Stx become running weighted sums, computed once for the whole signal), keep a cheap second pass only where residuals are large, and then add a light slope-consistency post-process: estimate noise sigma from the first-pass output's first differences, and wherever consecutive output differences are below ~0.5*sigma (i.e., statistically indistinguishable from noise), replace the output locally with a 3-tap running median. This "snaps" micro-fluctuations to a locally consistent value, directly reducing spurious slope reversals and false reversals without hurting tracking of genuine trends (median snapping only activates on sub-noise changes). The vectorization buys back the efficiency headroom so the overall runtime stays low while the smoothing pass reduces slope churn.
